```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
has_gg <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

This vignette walks through a typical analysis of the Florida Pasture Cube:

1. choose fields;
2. read their 5-day series;
3. look at a field;
4. relate its greenness to drought;
5. find the validation and benchmark tables.

It uses the small real extract shipped with the package, which holds nine fields from Hardee, DeSoto and
Highlands counties. With the full data downloaded by `fpc_download()`, drop the `dir = d` arguments.

```{r}
library(fpcubeR)
d <- fpc_example_dir()
```

## 1. Choose fields

`fpc_fields()` returns the fields as an `sf` object in EPSG:5070. The tiers differ in how sure we are that a
field is grazed:

- **A:** fields on parcels coded as grazing land.
- **B:** fields on other parcels that were mapped as pasture in nearly every year.
- **C:** open pasture in the official land-use maps that the Cropland Data Layer maps as woody or wetland.

```{r}
f <- fpc_fields(dir = d)
table(f$tier)
f[, c("field_id", "tier", "county", "area_ha", "hand_mean_m")]
```

Filters can be combined, and `geometry = FALSE` returns a plain data frame:

```{r}
fpc_fields(tier = c("A", "B"), county = "Hardee", geometry = FALSE, dir = d)[, c("field_id", "tier")]
```

## 2. Read the series

`fpc_composites()` reads one row per field and 5-day period. Gap-filled optical values are set to `NA`
unless you ask for them with `observed_only = FALSE`. They are built from the next observation, so they must
not enter forecasts or other causal analyses.

```{r}
x <- fpc_composites(f, vars = c("ndvi", "vv_db", "ppt_sum"), years = 2022, dir = d)
head(x)
mean(!is.na(x$ndvi))   # share of field-periods with an observed NDVI
```

`fpc_variables()` documents every variable:

```{r}
v <- fpc_variables(d)
v[v$group %in% c("radar", "weather"), c("name", "units", "description")]
```

## 3. Look at a field

```{r, eval = has_gg, fig.height = 4.5}
fpc_plot_field("FPC060780", vars = c("ndvi", "vv_db", "ppt_sum"), years = 2022:2023, dir = d)
```

The open circles are gap-filled values, drawn only to show the seasonal course. The per-acquisition records
behind the composites are in `fpc_observations()`:

```{r}
o <- fpc_observations("optical", fields = "FPC060780", years = 2022, dir = d)
nrow(o)
table(o$sensor)
```

## 4. Greenness and drought

`fpc_anomaly()` compares each value with the field's own climatology for the same time of year, and
`fpc_add_drought()` adds the county drought class valid on each date.

```{r}
x3 <- fpc_composites(f, vars = "ndvi", dir = d)
a <- fpc_add_drought(fpc_anomaly(x3, "ndvi", ref_years = 2021:2022, min_years = 2), dir = d)
aggregate(anomaly ~ usdm_class, a, function(z) round(median(z), 3))
```

```{r, eval = has_gg, fig.height = 3.5}
library(ggplot2)
a$drought <- factor(a$usdm_class, 0:5, c("none", "D0", "D1", "D2", "D3", "D4"))
ggplot(a[!is.na(a$anomaly), ], aes(drought, anomaly)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "County drought class", y = "NDVI anomaly", title = "Nine example fields, 2021-2023") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 5. Validation and benchmark tables

The release also holds the tables behind the validation and the benchmark of the paper, and the link of every
field to version 1.0. For example, the ESA WorldCover cover of the fields and the scores of task 1:

```{r}
w <- fpc_validation("worldcover_by_field", fields = f, dir = d)
w[, c("field_id", "grassland", "tree", "herbaceous_wetland")]
r <- fpc_benchmark("task1_results", dir = d)
r[r$split == "test" & r$horizon_days == 30, c("model", "rmse", "skill_vs_ref")]
```

`fpc_lineage()`, `fpc_validation()` and `fpc_benchmark()` without a table name list what is available.

## Working with the full data set

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fpc_download(c("fields", "composites", "labels"))   # about 2.4 GB
fpc_download("optical")                              # per-acquisition HLS records, 4 GB
fa <- fpc_fields(tier = "A")
x <- fpc_composites(fa, vars = c("ndvi", "ppt_sum"), from = "2022-01-01", to = "2023-12-31")
```

Reading all fields for one year gives about 4.6 million rows. Select the fields and variables you need, and
the readers then load only those parts of the files.
